title: Test Your Understanding: Multi-Region and Active-Active
description: Active-passive vs active-active, failover, conflicts, and residency — not just definitions.

questions.question: What is the main consistency advantage of active-passive (primary + DR) over active-active writes to the same rows?

options.text: A single write primary avoids cross-region write conflicts on the same record
Passive region serves all global writes

questions.explanation: With one primary accepting writes, you avoid two regions mutating the same row concurrently. Active-active requires explicit conflict handling; active-passive trades idle DR cost for simpler correctness.

questions.question: RPO (recovery point objective) measures:

options.text: How long until service is restored after failure
How much data loss is acceptable since the last replicated state

questions.explanation: RPO is the maximum acceptable data loss window (unreplicated writes). RTO is time to restore service. Async cross-region replication means failover may sacrifice recent writes unless sync or quorum writes are used.

questions.question: A user writes to the US primary, then immediately reads from an EU replica. They don't see their update. The most likely cause is:

options.text: Cross-region replication lag — read hit stale replica

questions.explanation: Async replication between regions takes time. Read-your-writes fails if reads go to a lagging replica. Mitigations: sticky region, read-after-write from primary, or version checks.

questions.question: Last-write-wins (LWW) conflict resolution is:

options.text: Simple but can silently drop concurrent updates

questions.explanation: LWW picks the highest timestamp/version. Concurrent edits lose one side's changes without notice. Fine for some caches; dangerous for collaborative or monetary state unless the domain accepts it.

questions.question: Routing all writes for `user:42` to a single home region based on hash is an example of:

options.text: Single writer per entity to reduce cross-region conflicts
Modulo sharding on a fixed N forever

questions.explanation: Home-region ownership ensures one region owns writes for a given key, enabling local reads with fewer concurrent cross-region mutations. Failover must transfer ownership carefully.

questions.question: For many global read-heavy apps, what often solves user-perceived latency WITHOUT active-active writes?

options.text: CDN + regional read replicas with a single or partitioned write path

questions.explanation: Edge caching and local reads address most latency pain. Multi-region active-active writes are for availability/consistency trade-offs that simpler patterns can't meet — not the first lever.

questions.question: During regional failover, split-brain risk means:

options.text: Both regions may believe they are primary and accept conflicting writes

questions.explanation: If US and EU both promote themselves primary without quorum/fencing, divergent writes corrupt data. Regional failover reuses the same coordination lessons as cluster leader election.

questions.question: Data residency requirements (e.g. keeping EU personal data in EU) are purely a legal concern and never affect system architecture.
questions.explanation: Residency drives region-scoped storage, replication boundaries, routing, and sometimes separate deployments. Engineering and legal design together — retrofitting is expensive.
